Early last week, Apple rolled out a carrier settings update for some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network to address mobile network issues they were experiencing. Apple is now pushing out another, separate carrier bundle update for devices running iOS 27.2 beta. Details below.

Apple releases AT&T carrier bundle update for iOS 27.2 beta

Last Friday, Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network were experiencing an issue that could cause their devices to lose mobile network service and be unable to make calls.

Apple said iOS 27.0.1, together with a new carrier settings update, was meant to prevent the issue from affecting other devices. However, iPhones that had already lost service would still require a hardware replacement.

Tonight, as spotted by Aaron Perris on X, Apple began pushing out another carrier bundle update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network, this time specifically targeting devices running the iOS 27.2 beta.

Reports of the issue first surfaced back in late September, when some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T discovered that their devices suddenly could not make or receive calls, send or receive texts, or use mobile data, with only "SOS" showing in the status bar.

Worth noting is that the issue only affected the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem in the US. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple's in-house C2 modem, was not affected.

The carrier settings update Apple pushed out last week bumped AT&T users running iOS 27.0 to version 72.1. However, users on the iOS 27.2 beta were still stuck on the older 72.0.2 carrier bundle.

Tonight's release is said to bump those devices up to carrier bundle version 72.0.3, most likely extending Apple's changes to AT&T's carrier settings to iPhone 18 Pro Max users testing the iOS 27.2 beta.
